subject: DPA review: tenant subprocessor zoning, on‑shore KMS & prompt/response entitlements
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@healthgrid.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.io>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: DPA asks (no-train commitment, subprocessors, KMS)

Alex — thanks for the demo last week. Procurement shared a draft DPA and there are three security/legal points we need clarified before we can push to our GC for signoff: 

1) No‑training / no‑derive: HealthGrid needs an explicit, machine-readable commitment that Customer Data will not be used to train, fine‑tune, or otherwise improve Provider models (including derivative datasets). We understand inference may involve ephemeral KV/cache but request explicit language and a description of retention TTLs.

2) Prompt/response entitlements: we require that prompt inputs and generated responses be considered Customer Data and that any intellectual property in responses be licensed to HealthGrid under the contract. Please confirm Redwood's standard position and whether you can add a clause to exclude response outputs from Provider product improvement.

3) Subprocessor zoning & key residency: HealthGrid operates across multiple regulated lines — we need: (a) a per‑tenant subprocessor map (CSV is fine), (b) the ability to require on‑shore key wrapping for a subset of tenant data, and (c) an approval gate for adding new subprocessors that process HealthGrid tenant data.

Attached: our procurement checklist and a proposed DPA redline (we kept the asks focused). Can you share: your current subprocessor inventory, SOC2 reports for relevant subprocessors, and the technical approach to KMS-onshore?

We'd like to conclude legal review by end of next week if possible.

Best,
Sara
Procurement Manager
HealthGrid

Attachments: procurement_checklist_HealthGrid.pdf (pdf), requested_dpa_redline.docx (docx)

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@healthgrid.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA asks (no-train commitment, subprocessors, KMS)

Sara — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. High level: we can meet each of these asks with a few guardrails and an operational plan. Quick answers up front: 

• No‑training: Redwood can commit to a contractual "No Model Training" clause for HealthGrid tenant traffic: Provider shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or improve models. We will add explicit TTLs for ephemeral KV caches (default 24 hours, configurable per‑tenant).

• Prompt/response entitlements: we propose a grant that gives HealthGrid an exclusive license to generated outputs for the term of the agreement and will exclude outputs from product improvement. We will add a narrow exception for aggregated telemetry (latency/error metrics) that contains no prompt/response text.

• Subprocessors & KMS: attaching our current subprocessor inventory (CSV) and a redline that includes an "on‑shore key wrapping" option — either Redwood manages a dedicated on‑shore KMS for that tenant or HealthGrid may bring‑your‑own‑key (BYOK) via a supported HSM/KMS integration. New subprocessors will be subject to a 30‑day approval/notice window for HealthGrid.

Next steps: Kim (cc'd) will provide proposed DPA language for the no‑train and outputs clauses; Ben will scope a short ops runbook (onboarding checklist and SOC2 links) we can share with your procurement team. Can we plan a quick call Wednesday to walk the redline and confirm the KMS approach?

Thanks — attaching our suggested DPA redline (HealthGrid_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) and the subprocessor inventory (subprocessors_inventory_20270515.csv).

— Alex
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: HealthGrid_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (pdf), subprocessors_inventory_20270515.csv (csv)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA asks (no-train commitment, subprocessors, KMS) — proposed legal language

On Mon, May 17, 2027 at 09:32 AM Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Sara — thanks for the clear notes and the redline. High level: we can meet each of these asks with a few guardrails and an operational plan.

Team — drafting notes below to use in the redline. Keeping the language narrow and operationally enforceable is important; avoid broad permanent IP assignments without corresponding controls. Proposed clauses: 

1) No Model Training (narrow): "Provider shall not use Customer Data, including prompt inputs and generated responses, to train, adapt, or improve any machine learning model or model weights used by Provider, now or in the future. Provider may use transient in‑memory KV caches and batching mechanisms for inference optimization provided such caches expire within a Tenant‑configurable TTL not to exceed 30 days, with a default of 24 hours unless Customer requests otherwise."

2) Output entitlements: "Provider grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, non‑exclusive license to generated outputs created from Customer Data during the term. Provider will not use generated outputs to improve Provider models. Provider reserves the right to collect non‑content telemetry (e.g., token counts, error rates, latency metrics) for service operation and billing."

3) Subprocessor gating & KMS residency: "Provider will supply an up‑to‑date subprocessor inventory and SOC2 attestations. For categorised regulated Tenant data, Customer may require on‑shore key wrapping or BYOK; Provider will support either path and will not onboard a new subprocessor to process regulated Tenant data without Customer's written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, such consent to be requested at least 30 days prior to onboarding."

4) Audit & evidence: add an audit rights paragraph limited to once per year, scoped to evidence necessary to validate the no‑train commitment (configurations, cache TTLs, and subprocessor access logs), subject to mutual NDAs and redaction for third‑party sensitive info.

Risks/notes: we should avoid granting exclusive ownership over model IP generated by Redwood for other customers; instead, deliver a strong license/entitlement to HealthGrid plus the onshore residency and gating controls. Ben — please confirm operational feasibility of the TTLs and the 30‑day gating.

— Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Li <sara.li@healthgrid.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthGrid Procurement <procurement@healthgrid.io>
Date: Wed, 18 May 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA asks (no-train commitment, subprocessors, KMS)

Alex / Kim — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the draft language. This is close to what we need. Two quick asks before I route to GC: 

• Can you change the TTL cap from "not to exceed 30 days" to "not to exceed 7 days" for regulated tenant categories? We have a regulatory requirement to limit transient caches to a shorter window for PHI.

• Please share SOC2 reports for any subprocessors in the CSV that are marked as "access to tenant payloads." Procurement attached our negotiated procurement checklist — I also dropped a DocuSign template (DocuSign_Link.txt) we typically use for rapid exchange.

If you can confirm the 7‑day TTL for regulated tenants and provide SOC2 PDFs, I'll aim to get this to legal the same day. Also ok with the proposed audit right once NDAs are in place.

Best,
Sara
Procurement Manager
HealthGrid
